task.description: Validate DDL-01, MIG-04, MIG-05, MIG-06 (all MUST) are ready for release. All prior gates PASSED, including one resolved rework cycle at Step 3b (a test-fixture defect in TC-MIG-04-03 that TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR correctly caught and TEST-DESIGNER fixed). Given that history, be thorough: read every AC in all 4 requirement bodies from docs/requirements.yaml and cross-check real test evidence, do not just trust the test report summary. Pay special attention to MIG-05 AC5 (documented non-testable-by-design, already accepted at Step 1b and Step 3b -- confirm this reasoning still holds and is not a cover for missing work) and MIG-06's open item (BACKEND-DEV flagged that route registration in main.zig uses a placeholder empty known_migration_ids and a no-op DdlStep since no real migration-file registry exists yet -- confirm this is genuinely within the design's accepted scope, not a silently incomplete implementation of an AC that should be release-blocking). Confirm migration idempotency (zig build migrate twice, clean no-op). This batch adds real HTTP endpoints (MIG-06) -- assess whether any NFR benchmark applies now that endpoints exist, or whether it's still N/A.
acceptance_criteria: All MUST requirement ACs have passing integration test evidence
No deferred/skipped coverage on any MUST requirement AC (except the already-accepted MIG-05 AC5 non-runtime-testable case)
MIG-06's known_migration_ids/DdlStep placeholder assessed as in-scope-deferred vs release-blocking

result.summary: Release APPROVED for Stage 16 (DDL-01, MIG-04, MIG-05, MIG-06). All ACs across all 4 requirements cross-checked against actual Zig test source (not just the test report): 21/21 DDL-01 unit tests, 9/9 MIG-04/MIG-05 integration tests, 6/6 MIG-06 integration tests, all independently re-run and matching the report exactly. MIG-05 AC5 non-testable-by-design reasoning re-confirmed by reading migration_fanout.zig directly: zero content-hash/immutability code exists, matching the design doc's disclosed Open Question 1. MIG-06's known_migration_ids placeholder in main.zig judged a legitimate, already-scoped integration-point deferral (design doc Open Question 2, accepted at Step 1b) -- handleRunMigration's own contract is correct and fully tested via test-supplied known_migration_ids; only the real on-disk registry is deferred, and the deferral is fail-safe (everything 404s as unknown) rather than silently permissive. zig build migrate run twice, both clean idempotent no-ops, exit 0. zig build bench run: all 5 existing NFR checks pass; HTTP-level route benchmarks judged N/A for this batch -- no HTTP-route bench harness exists anywhere in the codebase yet (pre-existing gap, not batch-specific), and HTTP NFR benchmarking is WF-04's dedicated Step 6, not every individual WF-02 batch, consistent with batch-0's own precedent.
